info.bio:
George Michael (East Finchley, Londres, Inglaterra, 25 de junio de 1963 - Goring-on-Thames, Oxfordshire, 25 de diciembre de 2016).

Su verdadero nombre era Georgios Kyriacos Panayiotou. Su padre es grecochipriota y su madre era inglesa. George comenzó su carrera formando una banda llamada The Executive con su mejor amigo Andrew Ridgeley, compañero de la Bushey Meads School.

No fue sino hasta que formó el dúo Wham! con Ridgeley, en 1981, que la fama llegó.

scenes.name: Naked funk: la era Reagan
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: La era del naked funk abarca las cimas de Prince, Michael Jackson y los dos mandatos de Reagan: recortes, desindustrialización, millones de sin techo, la «guerra contra las drogas» en lugar de contra la pobreza y, desde 1982, el crack. La música negra se volvió narcisista y escapista, del «yo primero»; las bandas, demasiado caras para la ciudad. La industria ofrecía estereotipos (banda pop, crooner, banda funk guarra, según Jon Pareles), MTV no ponía vídeos negros hasta Thriller y Jackson y Prince marcaron las cuotas del crossover. En 1975 trece números 1 R&B eran funk; en 1985 diecisiete de veinte eran baladas. Warner echó a Clinton y CBS sepultó «Pumpin’ It Up»; murieron o se convirtieron Hathaway, Joe Tex, Marvin Gaye, Al Green, Larry Graham. Las máquinas sustituyeron vientos, órgano (el Yamaha DX7), batería y bajo: solo sobrevivió la guitarra rítmica sobre el bajo sintetizado y la palmada electrónica. La insinuación dejó paso al sexo explícito sin cerebro («Do Me Baby», «Beep a Freak»), y llegaron el bass de Miami (2 Live Crew), Egyptian Lover, el New Jack Swing de Teddy Riley y la farsa de Milli Vanilli. Los funkers de verdad abandonaron la radio: el underground (hip hop, go-go) llevó el funk adelante.

scenes.name: Segunda invasión británica y MTV
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1982 el new pop deja de ser un sueño de periodistas: «Don't You Want Me», «Tainted Love» y «The Look of Love» anuncian una nueva invasión, y en 1983 la segunda camada (Duran Duran, Culture Club, Wham!, Eurythmics, Thompson Twins) conquista Estados Unidos gracias a MTV, canal ideado por Michael Nesmith que, sin vídeos americanos, dependía de los británicos, más videogénicos y cultivados en el estilo («I want my MTV»). A Flock of Seagulls, Altered Images («Happy Birthday»), Simple Minds («Promised You a Miracle», New Gold Dream), Haircut 100, Kajagoogoo; Bowie se broncea con «Let's Dance». El new pop reexporta música negra (Chic, P-Funk, Quincy Jones) a la América blanca. En el Reino Unido, 1983 se vive en cambio como un año infausto: reelección de Thatcher, «Kill Ugly Pop» en las paredes y la vuelta de la conciencia social.

podcast.title: Clive Davis Collaboration Call (1986)
podcast.body: During his pivot to a solo career, Michael received a call from Clive Davis, who proposed a duet with Aretha Franklin on "I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me)," a song Davis envisioned as a duet. "Michael got a call from Clive Davis, who had a song he thought George could sing on with The Queen of Soul."

podcast.title: Emerging from Wham! (1986)
podcast.body: George Michael was emerging from the shadow of Wham!, the globally successful pop duo he formed with Andrew Ridgeley, which had conquered charts, toured China, and blended British new wave with blue-eyed soul on hits like "Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go." "British pop singer George Michael was emerging from the shadow of WAM, the pop duo he'd formed with Andrew Ridgley five years earlier."

podcast.title: Wham! Breakup (Summer 1986)
podcast.body: Wham! officially broke up in the summer of 1986 following a farewell concert at Wembley Stadium, after which Michael began work on his solo debut album. podcast.title: Detroit Studio Experience (1987)
podcast.body: Michael flew on the Concorde from London to Detroit to record with Aretha Franklin, expressing excitement, nervousness, and awe of "The Queen" during the session. He managed to hold his own vocally against Franklin, similar to Annie Lennox's performance a year earlier. "Michael flew on the Concorde from London to Detroit, excited, nervous, and in awe of The Queen."

podcast.title: Imperial Genre Flex
podcast.body: George Michael utilized his imperial phase after the success of his "Faith" album to experiment with a completely different sound, releasing "Kissing a Fool" as a cocktail jazz single in late 1988. This "sophisticated pop" track, despite being incongruous on Top 40 radio, made the top five, illustrating his artistic license during his imperial peak. "Michael decided he'd try getting on the radio with his take on cocktail jazz. Talk about a flex Kissing a Fool made the top five on the hot 100."

podcast.title: Redefined Image (1980s)
podcast.body: George Michael's iconic music video for "Faith," featuring him in a leather jacket, tight jeans, and facial stubble, redefined his image for the remainder of the 1980s. "This homage to Rockabilly came with an iconic music video, George in a leather jacket, tight jeans, and facial stubble that redefined his image for the rest of the decade."
